# YallaFlow 1.0

**Give AI your project, not just your prompt.**

Your coding agent is already smart. YallaFlow gives it durable project memory, the right engineering workflow for each request, and evidence that the work is actually done — without you carrying all of that in every prompt.

> You describe the intent. YallaFlow supplies the project.

This is YallaFlow's first public, stable release.

## What YallaFlow gives your coding agent

- **Durable project memory** — reviewed, evidence-backed knowledge of the project (architecture, rules, decisions) that every session and every teammate starts from, with freshness tracking so stale knowledge is revalidated instead of trusted.
- **Adaptive engineering workflows** — a bug, a feature, an investigation, and a refactor each get the lifecycle they need, proportional to their scope.
- **Evidence-backed delivery** — "done" requires fresh verification evidence, and feature work is checked against the intent you approved.
- **Session and agent continuity** — close the chat, open a new one, or switch between Claude Code and Codex; the engineering state lives with the project.
- **Shared project intelligence through Git** — one reviewed understanding of the project for the whole team, shared through ordinary commits.

## Start

```bash
npm install -g yallaflow
cd your-project
yallaflow init
```

Then open Claude Code or Codex in the project and describe the work:

```text
Fix invoice totals.
```

No "use YallaFlow", no workflow choice, no setup prompts.

## Existing projects

The first time you ask for real work on an existing codebase, the agent builds an evidence-backed understanding of the project first — focused by your request — without changing application code or copying secrets. It shows you what it found and what it could not inspect. Reply **Approve**, and your original request continues automatically. This happens once per project: understand once, share automatically, revalidate precisely.

## Teams

**Developers work with Git. Agents work with YallaFlow.**

A maintainer runs `yallaflow init`, approves the project understanding, runs `yallaflow shared enable`, and commits `.yallaflow/`. Everyone else just pulls, describes their task to their agent, and pushes. Work IDs are branch-safe, knowledge learned on a branch travels with it, project memory is integrated in one place, and `yallaflow shared check` is a read-only CI gate for any CI provider.

## Privacy

YallaFlow is local-first. There is no YallaFlow server or account, no telemetry, and no LLM or network calls: your code, project memory, and sources never leave your machine through YallaFlow. Recognizable secret values are redacted before anything is persisted. YallaFlow never commits, pushes, or merges for you.

## Compatibility and requirements

- Node.js **>= 20.16.0** (for the CLI only; your project can use any stack).
- First-party setup for **Claude Code** and **Codex**; other agents can follow `.yallaflow/AGENT.md`.
- From 1.0.0, YallaFlow follows **Semantic Versioning**: existing workspaces stay readable, work items keep their pinned behavior, released skill instructions are immutable, and historical work is never silently rewritten.
- Coming from `0.3.10-internal.4`: nothing to do. From an earlier prerelease: run `yallaflow upgrade plan` (typically `yallaflow agent refresh`) — see the upgrade guide.
- Known limitations: Windows is not verified yet; no OCR for images or scanned PDFs; agent compliance with workflow gates is guidance, not enforcement; one moderate, mitigated dependency advisory (`file-type` via `officeparser`).
